column3: It directly contrasts one upon clear proof with one whose evil deed is beautified and who follows desire.
It distinguishes good and evil deeds in recompense but does not address evil being perceived as good.
It links mistaken disbelief to abiding regret and closes with God's sight of what people do.
It repeats the focus ayah's formulation that God misguides and guides whom He wills, with accountability for deeds.
Its discussion of unresponsive false gods does not materially clarify the focus relation.
It explicitly says the disbelievers' evil deeds were beautified to them and associates that with misguidance.
It joins beautified plotting, obstruction from the path, and the lack of a guide for one God misguides.
God's sole control over mercy is only a broad local parallel to divine direction in the focus.
Replacing evil with good concerns repentance, not the deceptive beautification of evil.
It directly states that God misguides whom He wills and guides those who turn back to Him.
The true beauty of God's names offers only a loose contrast to falsely beautified evil.
Deniers encounter regret over what they neglected, illuminating the focus's warning not to grieve over them.
Those denying evil deeds are answered by God's full knowledge of what they did.
Its contrast between two seas and their visible benefits only loosely echoes appearance and evaluation.
It pairs personal guidance or error with the Prophet's lack of guardianship over people.
Pharaoh's evil deed is beautified to him and he is turned from the path.
God's knowledge of every pregnancy and lifespan gives a local parallel to the focus's comprehensive knowledge.
A good reward for righteous deeds contrasts only broadly with the focus's evil deeds.
The same sign becomes a means by which God guides many and misguides many according to their response.
Its instruction for gracious speech when unable to give does not clarify the focus relation.
It identifies the revelation as a source of regret for disbelievers.
It connects disciplined sight and conduct with God's knowledge of what people do.
It contrasts upright words and righteous action with evil plotting in the same local passage.
Those seeking to mislead others ultimately mislead only themselves, a related reversal of direction.
Followers are shown their deeds as regrets, directly resonating with the focus's warning against self-consuming grief.
The nearby warning against worldly deception directly frames the focus's theme of deceptive appearance.
It states that guidance and error return to each person's own self and that the Prophet is not their guardian.
God's call to peace and guidance to the straight path parallels the focus's divine guidance clause.
The terror of the Hour and disrupted nursing imagery do not clarify the focus relation.
It depicts a person wrongly treating relief as proof that evil has permanently gone away.
Its shifting light and darkness portray unstable perception and divine power over sight, but not beautified evil.
The local call to remember the sole Creator only broadly contrasts with being turned away from truth.
Untiring angelic worship does not materially clarify the focus relation.
A community's ungrateful action brings a reversal from security to hardship, showing the consequence of its deeds.
Their claim that they would be better guided reverses into stronger aversion when the warner arrives.
It describes people whose efforts are lost while they think they are doing good, a direct perceptual reversal.
Seeing a person in Hell is actual disclosure, not the focus's false evaluation of evil.
Attributing partners after receiving a good gift is only a broad instance of distorted religious judgment.
Abraham's voluntary turning toward his Lord and expectation of guidance provides a positive directional contrast.
It contrasts a good divine promise with transient worldly enjoyment but not a false perception of deeds.
The rest and permanence of Paradise do not materially clarify the focus relation.
The failed search for flaws in creation does not address evil being made to appear good.
It repeats that God misguides and guides whom He wills while distinguishing belief, doubt, and disbelief.
God's gift of judgment and knowledge to one who does good is only broadly related to evaluating deeds.
Seeing even an atom's weight of good deed loosely counters the concealment of a deed's true value.
The pilgrimage rite and voluntary good do not clarify the focus relation.
Its revival image and resurrection analogy do not materially develop deceptive perception or guidance.
Seeing blessing and great dominion concerns true reward rather than mistaking evil for good.
Mary's favorable reception and provision do not clarify the focus relation.
The warning about the Hour's earthquake does not materially clarify the focus relation.
It warns of the Day of Regret while people remain heedless and disbelieving.
It closely parallels the command not to consume oneself with grief because people refuse belief.
God's origination and creation of angels do not materially clarify the focus relation.
The command to go to Pharaoh does not clarify the focus relation.
It condemns sinful speech and illicit gain while rebuking leaders who fail to restrain such deeds.
God's knowledge of everything and its record in a book parallels the focus's assurance that He knows their acts.
Its recompense for those who do good only broadly contrasts with wrongly valued evil deeds.
Evildoers face punishment for what they earned, preserving the true moral value of their actions.
Cosmic alternation and the impotence of invoked others do not materially clarify the focus relation.
Its rejected contrast reading gives no positive support for the focus relation.
It rejects obeying pressure toward associating partners without knowledge and promises an account of deeds.
Breaking the idols into fragments does not materially clarify the focus relation.
The heavens' true ornament provides only a loose contrast to the false beautification of evil.
God's knowledge of what people do supports the focus's closing assurance, though the instruction concerns etiquette.
The progressive showing of signs until truth becomes clear counteracts mistaken perception only indirectly.
It affirms that the heart did not falsify what it saw, offering a contrast between true and distorted perception.
The metaphor of a good loan and multiplied reward does not clarify the focus relation.
The oath by smoothly moving things does not materially clarify the focus relation.
Joseph's brothers wrongly judge their father to be in clear error, a limited example of false assessment.
It attributes evil affecting a person to the self while retaining God as witness, related to accountable action.
The oath by distributors of command does not materially clarify the focus relation.
The evildoer will see even an atom's weight of evil, exposing a deed's actual consequence.
It records forgotten covenant and resulting hostility, but offers only a distant relation to the focus's deeds.
The creation and benefits of livestock do not materially clarify the focus relation.
Paradisal adornment is a true reward for faith and good deeds, loosely contrasting deceptive adornment.
Wealth spent to obstruct God's path becomes a source of regret for its owners.
It rebukes those doing evil who think they can escape God and calls their judgment evil.
It closely addresses the Prophet's self-exhaustion over people's refusal to believe.
It contrasts believers who know the Hour is true with deniers in distant misguidance.
It explicitly says desires are made attractive to people while directing value toward the better final return.
The self-reproaching soul alone does not materially clarify the focus relation.
God clarifies the ruling so people do not go astray and closes with His knowledge of everything.
The temperate conditions of Paradise do not materially clarify the focus relation.
Personal obligation while encouraging believers loosely parallels limits on bearing others' response.
It tells believers to attend to themselves: others' error does not harm one who is guided.
It corrects a visual assumption about mountains and closes with God's knowledge of human deeds.
It explicitly says Satan beautified prior peoples' deeds, with their resulting allegiance and punishment.
It contrasts a false deifying claim with God's complete knowledge of what is hidden within a person.
It warns that excess or stinginess leaves one blameworthy and regretful, a limited grief parallel.
God's sight of what people do appears in a legal instruction but is only a broad parallel.
God preserves the reward of those who excel in deeds, only broadly contrasting evil's false appearance.
The good permanent abode is a true positive evaluation, not a deceptive perception of action.
Pilgrimage completion and its compensations do not materially clarify the focus relation.
Noah denies being astray and grounds his direction in his mission from the Lord.
Those who lied about God are visibly exposed and judged, revealing the true outcome of hidden falsehood.
Even after seeing the signs of innocence, authorities choose imprisonment, showing action against known truth.
Degrees and full recompense according to deeds only broadly preserve their true evaluation.
The certain sight of Hell is disclosure of reality but not mistaken valuation of one's deed.
Qarun's collapse exposes the failure of apparent worldly power, only indirectly related to the focus.
God's hearing and sight provide only a general parallel to His knowledge of what people do.
It explicitly says Satan made their deeds seem fair to them, directly paralleling evil being beautified.
It states that every community's work has been made pleasing to it, directly addressing the perceived goodness of deeds.
It contrasts life and light with darkness and says the disbelievers' deeds have been made fair to them.
It says alleged partners made the killing of children seem alluring to polytheists, a concrete case of evil beautified.
Those taking devils as protectors instead of God think they are rightly guided, closely matching false self-assessment.
It describes people who reject the way of right guidance and take the way of error when they see it.
Satan made the disbelievers' deeds seem fair and then abandoned them, directly pairing beautification with deception.
Satan admits he only called and deceived people, locating their response within a misleading invitation rather than coercion.
Satan vows to make evil attractive on earth and lead people astray, directly naming both focus themes.
The Samiri says his own soul made his act attractive to him, a specific instance of an evil act appearing good.
Whoever takes Satan as a patron is led astray and driven toward the punishment of the Blaze.
The deeds of disbelievers are compared to a mirage mistaken for water, a direct image of false evaluation.
Taking one's desire as a god exposes a source of moral distortion closely related to following beautified evil.
Satan made the people's deeds fair to them and barred them from the path, directly matching the focus structure.
Following desire without guidance from God gives a direct counterpoint to the focus's guidance and misguidance.
Wrongdoers follow their desires without knowledge, followed immediately by the question of who can guide one God misguides.
It condemns misleading others from God's path without knowledge, a related misuse of desire and appearance.
It identifies Satan as an open enemy whose worship led many people astray.
Following desire is said to lead one astray from God's path, clarifying a mechanism behind moral error.
It repeats that no one can guide the person whom God lets go astray.
It complements the focus by affirming that no one can mislead the person whom God guides.
It says that what lay before and behind them was made fair to them, directly describing comprehensive deceptive beautification.
Turning away from God's remembrance results in a devil companion, directly linking neglect to misleading influence.
Devils turn people from the path while those people think they are rightly guided, an especially close perceptual parallel.
It combines taking desire as a god, divine misguidance, and sealing of hearing, heart, and sight.
Those who turn back after guidance are described as having Satan make their course fair to them.
It says an evil thought about God was made fair in their hearts, directly naming beautified evil judgment.
It contrasts conjecture and desire with guidance that has come from the Lord.
Forgetting God leads people to forget themselves, a related account of self-destructive moral blindness.
When people deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate further, closely paralleling divine misguidance after turning away.
